outline: 643 Area of Composite Figures with Special Quadrilaterals

examples.solution_text:
Use the two complete diagonals.
$\begin{aligned}A&=\frac{xy}{2}\\A&=\frac{13\times7}{2}\\A&=\frac{91}{2}\\A&=45.5\text{ cm}^2\end{aligned}$

Add the two parts of the vertical diagonal first.
$\begin{aligned}y&=4+11\\y&=15\text{ cm}\\A&=\frac{xy}{2}\\A&=\frac{9\times15}{2}\\A&=\frac{135}{2}\\A&=67.5\text{ cm}^2\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A kite has diagonals of length $2.6$ cm and $37$ mm. Find its area, in square centimetres.
examples.solution_text:
Write both diagonal lengths in centimetres before substituting.
$\begin{aligned}y&=37\div10\\y&=3.7\text{ cm}\\A&=\frac{xy}{2}\\A&=\frac{2.6\times3.7}{2}\\A&=\frac{9.62}{2}\\A&=4.81\text{ cm}^2\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A rhombus has a side of length $8.2$ cm and perpendicular height $6.3$ cm. Explain why $\frac{8.2\times6.3}{2}$ does not give its area.
examples.solution_text: The formula $A=\frac{xy}{2}$ uses two diagonals, joining opposite corners. Here $8.2$ cm is a side and $6.3$ cm is a perpendicular height. They are not the diagonals, so they cannot be used as $x$ and $y$.

Double each labelled half to find the complete diagonals.
$\begin{aligned}x&=2\times6\\x&=12\text{ cm}\\y&=2\times8\\y&=16\text{ cm}\\A&=\frac{xy}{2}\\A&=\frac{12\times16}{2}\\A&=96\text{ cm}^2\end{aligned}$

Add the rod lengths along each complete diagonal.
$\begin{aligned}x&=20+20\\x&=40\text{ cm}\\y&=20+40\\y&=60\text{ cm}\\A&=\frac{xy}{2}\\A&=\frac{40\times60}{2}\\A&=1200\text{ cm}^2\end{aligned}$

Use the diagonals, $12$ cm and $9$ cm. The $7.5$ cm side is not a diagonal.
$\begin{aligned}A&=\frac{xy}{2}\\A&=\frac{12\times9}{2}\\A&=54\text{ cm}^2\end{aligned}$
